parole.testo: Of debated origin: # From Proto-Finno-Ugric *kerɜ- (“to burp”) + -ődzik (frequentative-reflexive suffix). Related to Northern Mansi кēральт (kēralʹt, “burp, belch”). # From a Turkic language, ultimately from Proto-Turkic *kēb- (“to chew”). Compare Turkish gevmek (“to chew”).

parole.significato: cloth (a piece of cloth used for cleaning)
parole.testo: Uncertain. Perhaps from Proto-Finno-Ugric *raćɜ (“rag”). Possibly from Turkic, compare Old Turkic [script needed] (uruŋu), Proto-Slavic *xorǫgy, Mongolian оронго (orongo).

parole.significato: master (someone who has control over something or someone)
parole.testo: Of debated origin: # From Proto-Finno-Ugric *urɜ (“man, male”). # Borrowed from a Turkic language before the times of the Hungarian conquest of the Carpathian Basin (at the turn of the 9th and 10th centuries), from Proto-Turkic *ūŕ (“master, craftsman”).
